input.rationale: Continuing the safety-axis lead from the answered reordering question with the two faults it did not cover, as its discriminator recorded: duplication of replication messages, and replay of a replaced leader's messages after the rest of the cluster has moved to a newer ballot. The probe reuses the same in-process driver and adds a transport fault layer (hold-from, duplicate-to, capture-first-AcceptDecide, replay-held). Locally all three cases behave as the source account predicts - control, duplication of every message addressed to node 2, and a takeover where 507 retained messages from the old leader were replayed after the heal - each ending with the same decided values (1,2,3,7,8,9) on all three nodes, and in the stale case all three nodes following node 3 afterwards, so the submitted execution is a bounded negative pair on these faults; the receipt is the evidence, not this local run.

investigations.question: In the core crate, do two faults the captured suites do not exercise preserve agreement and progress: (a) every replication message addressed to one follower delivered twice, and (b) a leader cut off from both followers while they take over, after which the replaced leader's retained messages are replayed to them once the link is restored?
investigations.hypothesis: Provisional: a duplicate carries a sequence number the follower has already consumed, so `check_msg_status` classifies it as outdated and the message is ignored, while a replaced leader's messages carry a ballot below the followers' promises and are rejected by `check_valid_ballot`; in both cases the nodes should still agree on the decided values and keep deciding new entries.
investigations.discriminator: The submitted three-case probe. It changes the judgment if the duplication or replay case ends with differing decided values across nodes, if the expected entries are not all decided, or if the control case diverges (which would point at the harness). It does not change the judgment if the fault never actually took effect, which the outcome events report explicitly.

scope.description: Three runs of one cluster shape with three real `OmniPaxos` instances driven directly through the public API in a single process (in-process delivery, node 1 the elected leader, node 2 the follower under observation, node 3 the third acceptor). All runs first decide entries 1..=3 as a baseline. Case A then decides 7 and 8 with no fault. Case B delivers every message addressed to node 2 twice while 7 and 8 are decided. Case C cuts node 1 off from both followers so that they elect node 3, lets node 3 decide 7 and 8, then restores the link and replays every message node 1 had sent while cut off, before deciding a final entry 9 through the current leader.
assumptions: Duplicate delivery and delayed delivery of already-sent messages are permitted faults; the core carries sequence numbers for the first and ballot checks for the second, and no caller duty in the docs rules them out.
Faults are applied in the transport only: no target logic is modified, and the leader is unaware of duplication, holding or replay.
Logical ticks driven by the harness exercise the election and resend timeouts deterministically rather than by wall-clock timing.
The instances run with batch_size 1, majority quorum and no snapshots, so decisions are observable immediately through `read_decided_suffix`.
excluded: Any claim about message corruption, reordering (probed separately) or storage faults.
Any claim about the actor layer: the probe drives the core crate directly.
Any claim about occurrence rates: one schedule per case.

parameters.duplication: case B: every message addressed to node 2 delivered twice
parameters.stale_replay: case C: messages from node 1 held while it is cut off, then replayed after the heal

experiment.prefix: For each case: build one `OmniPaxos<TestEntry, MemoryStorage<TestEntry>>` per node id (configuration_id 1, election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, node 1 leader_priority 1), elect node 1 by calling `try_become_leader()` and pumping until node 2 reports it as the accepted leader, append entries 1..=3 on node 1 and pump until every node has decided at least 3, then emit the admission event. Case A appends 7 and 8 on node 1. Case B sets the transport to deliver every message addressed to node 2 twice and then appends 7 and 8 on node 1. Case C sets the transport to hold every message sent by node 1, pumps until a node other than 1 reports itself as the accepted leader, appends 7 and 8 on that new leader, pumps, then clears the hold, replays all retained messages and pumps again. Finally append entry 9 through the current leader and pump fifteen rounds; then read each node's decided suffix and emit, under the mode-specific event name, the decided values and indexes per node, whether all three nodes' decided values are equal, whether exactly the expected entries were decided, how many messages were replayed, and each node's current leader.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs are produced by the target: the follower's sequence-number check decides what a duplicate means, and `check_valid_ballot` decides what a replaced leader's message means; the harness only chooses the delivery schedule and never inspects or repairs protocol state.

investigations.question: In the async actor layer, when an entry is accepted at a log index by the leader it was assigned to but is then dropped by a later leader change before decision, what resolution does the originating `append_notify` receive once the origin's local decided index reaches that index, and what does that resolution establish about the caller's entry?

investigations.question: In the core crate, when the cluster configuration contains node ids that are not contiguous, can the leader ever advance the compacted index with `trim` once every configured server has decided an entry, and does the documented `trim(Some(idx))` repair path make progress?

investigations.discriminator: Settled: four id sets and seven comparisons, with the snapshot boundary measured. Only same-cause variants remain (contiguous ids starting above 1 in a larger cluster, trimming after part of the log is already snapshotted), which would not change the account.

scope.description: One real in-process cluster shape (three OmniPaxos actors over an in-memory transport, majority quorum, batch_size 1, node 1 forced into the leader role), run three times with different admissions. Modes B and C: node 1's links to both followers are cut in both directions, node 1 - still the leader in the accept phase - takes entry 11 (so it can only be accepted locally and assigned an index), the two followers elect node 3, which decides entry 22 at the same first index, and node 1 is then reconnected so the new leader re-synchronizes it. B and C differ only in the actor tick period (2 ms vs 80 ms), which controls whether a drain_notifiers pass can run between the origin's promise change and its decided-index advance.
assumptions: Message loss/partition is a permitted fault for this protocol; the core tolerates lost messages via its resend path, and the harness drops whole messages inside the transport without adding backpressure.
Each node is a real OmniPaxos instance with MemoryStorage, batch_size 1 and a majority quorum, driven only through the public actor handle; no target logic is modified.

Node 1 carries leader_priority 1 so the pre-partition leader is stable; a higher priority only breaks ties at equal ballot number, and in modes B/C the followers reach a strictly higher ballot number through the election-timeout takeover path, so the priority cannot prevent the new election.

drain_notifiers runs only from the tick branch, so the resolution instant is quantised by tick_period; the gap between the origin's Prepare handling and the AcceptSync that follows it is one round trip (about 2-4 ms here).
excluded: Any claim about entries other than the two submitted values (11 by the origin, 22 by the new leader).
Any claim about transports, runtimes or timings other than the in-process in-memory transport used here.
Durable/crash recovery: the origin is re-synchronized in-process, it is not restarted, so no storage-persistence claim follows from these cases.

basis.prefix: Per case: build three OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..3, configuration_id 1, nodes [1,2,3], MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, election_tick_timeout 3, node 1 leader_priority 1) and spawn each as an actor through spawn_actor with a tokio-backed AsyncRuntime adapter (tick_period per case, egress_period 1 ms). Wire every node's outgoing_messages() receiver into a task that consults a per-direction block set and, unless the link is blocked, delivers the message with peer.handle_incoming(). Admission: call handles[1].try_become_leader() until all three nodes report current_leader() == (1, true) and still do so after four election timeouts; emit the admission event with the mode. Mode A: await handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)) and then read the origin's decided suffix. Modes B/C: block (1,2) and (1,3) both ways, spawn handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)) as a task, sleep one tick period, wait until nodes 2 and 3 both report a leader other than 1 with accepted=true, await handles[new_leader].append_notify(TestEntry(22)), then unblock both links and await the origin's future. Emit new_leader_elected, new_leader_append (with the new leader's decided values) and notify_resolution, the last carrying the resolved variant (ok / superseded / timeout / ...), the assigned index, the decided entry at that index and, only when that index was actually observed in the decided log, whether it equals the submitted value.
basis.responsibility: The decisive inputs are produced by the target itself: the actor assigns the caller's entry an index from its own local accept as leader, records the assignment as (index, ballot) with no entry identity, and drain_notifiers derives the resolution from the local decided index alone, evaluating the Ok arm before the ballot-change arm. The caller supplies only the entry value.
